title: Scoped Threads
summary: `thread::scope` guarantees all spawned threads finish before the scope ends, allowing threads to borrow stack data.
lecture: Standard threads created with `thread::spawn` must own their data or hold 'static references because the parent frame might end while the thread is running.
`thread::scope` introduces a bounded scope. All threads spawned on the scope handle are guaranteed to join before `thread::scope` returns.
Because the child threads cannot outlive the scope, they can safely borrow non-'static data from the surrounding stack frame according to standard Rust borrowing rules.

example.caption: The thread borrows s without cloning or moving.
